question: Solve \(\frac{x-1}{2}-\frac{2x+1}{3}=1\). (Enter only the value of \(x\).)
solution: Multiplying both sides by 6 (note that the 1 on the right must also be multiplied by 6) gives \(3(x-1)-2(2x+1)=6\), yielding \(3x-3-4x-2=6\), or \(-x-5=6\), so \(x=-11\).
